SyncGap0: 0 - off (fastest, tiles may differ in tone)
TipSyncGap:
Real-CUGAN only. A big picture is converted in pieces (the Split size); without this, neighbouring pieces can differ slightly in tone (faint squares, e.g. in a sky). Sync gap gives all pieces the same colour measurements:
0 - off: fastest, pieces may differ.
1 - accurate: the best match, the slowest.
2 - rough: faster.
3 - very rough (default): fast and already seamless - keep this.

MessageScaleNumFormatError:
<Width> and <Height> accept whole numbers only (0-9), e.g. 1920 or 1080.
Other characters are not supported.
MessageScaleWHFormatError:
<Width>x<Height> accepts only the form <width>x<height> with numbers, e.g. 1920x1080 or 2560x1440.
Other characters are not supported.

TipVramLimit:
The most GPU memory (VRAM) RePicturer may use, as a share of the memory that is free
when a conversion starts - not of the whole card. Example: 16 GB card, 12 GB free, 60 % = 7.2 GB.
20 - 60 % is a safe range: it leaves room for Windows, the browser and games, and avoids
out-of-memory errors and crashes. Go above 60 % only when nothing else uses the GPU.
An image that runs out is retried up to 3 times with a smaller Split size. Default 60 %.

TipRamLimit:
The most RAM the pictures in progress may use, as a share of the RAM that is free
when a conversion starts - not of all RAM. Example: 32 GB RAM, 20 GB free, 60 % = 12 GB.
20 - 60 % is a safe range: Windows and your other programs keep enough memory, and the PC
does not slow down or freeze. Go above 60 % only when nothing else is running.
When the limit is reached the next pictures wait; a single picture bigger than the limit fails. Default 60 %.

TipProcessingUnit:
Which part of the computer runs the AI.
GPU (graphics card): runs on Vulkan - fast. Works with NVIDIA, AMD and Intel, no CUDA needed.
CPU (processor): works without Vulkan - much slower, but on any computer.
Auto: the GPU, or the CPU when no GPU with Vulkan is found.
